description: Declare that the GAME serves a capability itself instead of a kit (GameProjectDoc.hostProvides), as the engine host serves physics.character: the user's own Godot / Unity / Unreal / Bevy terrain answers world.ground, its own camera camera.*… With the declaration the kits that require it keep working without a provider kit (none is added, none is removed with its dependents) and remove_kit removes that provider kit ALONE in the same revision. The game must then serve it at run time (GDScript host.provide_service("world.ground", obj), Unity Provide, Unreal ProvideService, C gfk_provide, Rust Host::provide — gripforge_docs topic engine-interop); a kit that asks it before it is served logs a warning naming it. Without add/remove it lists { hostProvides, hostable: { <kit>: capabilities the game could serve in its place } }. remove withdraws a declaration: the default provider kit comes back. dry_run=true previews. Then re-run game-attach in the engine project. 0 credits.

add.description: Capabilities the game serves from now on, e.g. ["world.ground"] (any version) or ["world.ground@1.0.0"].

dry_run.description: true to return the plan without writing.

project_id.description: Game Kit project id (gkp_…). Not a dedicated-server project (gpj_…) nor a Library item.

prune.description: true to also drop the auto-installed provider kits nothing needs any more.

reason.description: One sentence recorded in the project history.

remove.description: Capabilities a kit serves again (its default provider is installed back).

remove_kit.description: A provider kit to remove alone in the same revision (e.g. world.scene_ground); without add, the capabilities it provides to its dependents are declared.

workspace_id.description: Workspace authorized by the current key. Never infer another user’s workspace.

name: gripforge_game_host_provides
title: Capabilities the game serves itself
